context: I Observation 14. Let G0 be the subgraph of G induced by a node set V 0 ⊆ V and let 0 vmax ∈ V 0 be the node with the highest rank in the contraction order among all nodes in V 0 . Then the number of nodes in V 0 with their shortest path towards vmax 0 being completely 0 0 contained in G is a lower bound for |ISS(vmax )|. To get a lower bound which adheres to all possible contraction orders we need to deal with the fact that we do not know which node in V 0 will become vmax 0 . To make the bound more general, we can iterate through all nodes v ∈ V and compute the number of nodes in V 0 0 with the shortest path towards v being completely contained in G0 , keeping track of the minimum. We call this value the minimum shortest path tree size in G0 or misp(G0 ). I Theorem 15. For any β ∈ (0, 1], let G be a collection of subgraphs of G with misp(G0 ) ≥ βn for all G0 ∈ G. Furthermore, let H be a minimum HittingSet for the set system (V, G). Then it yields Savg ≥ β|H|.
